about.title: Murrieta Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails in an ordinary Murrieta home, garage, or backyard can change a family's year. Space heaters, e-bike batteries, pressure cookers, children's car seats, power tools bought along Murrieta Hot Springs Road — any of them can carry a design flaw, a manufacturing slip, or a missing warning that the buyer had no way to see. Riverside County residents also spend a lot of time behind the wheel, and vehicle components matter: in 2025 the city recorded 426 injury collisions and 595 people injured, and in some crashes an airbag, tire, or seatback defect is part of the story on roads like Clinton Keith or Winchester. California's strict liability rule is built for this situation. You generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the item was defective and that the defect hurt you. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who handles defective product claims, works on contingency, and can help make sure the product is preserved before anything gets thrown away.

whyChoose.title: Why Murrieta Residents Use LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict liability works in your favor
items.desc: The attorneys in our network understand that California generally requires proof of a defect and causation, not proof of negligence. That framing shapes how a Murrieta claim is investigated from day one.

items.title: Evidence gets protected early
items.desc: The product itself is usually the single most important piece of evidence. A prompt attorney connection helps ensure the item, packaging, receipts, and photos are preserved rather than discarded or returned to the store.

items.title: Every responsible party is considered
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the retailer that sold the item in or near Murrieta may all bear responsibility. An independent attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim instead of leaving that to guesswork.

items.question: I was in a crash on Clinton Keith Road and I think the airbag never deployed. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. The other driver may be responsible for the collision, while the vehicle or airbag manufacturer may be responsible for the added harm a defect caused. Do not let the car be salvaged or repaired before an attorney has a chance to review it, because the vehicle is the key evidence for the product side of the claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Usually not. Under California's strict liability rule, the focus is on whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and whether that defect caused your injury. The maker's state of mind is generally not the central question, which is one reason these claims differ from ordinary negligence cases.

items.question: I threw away the box and the receipt. Can I still pursue a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. The product itself matters far more than the packaging, so keep it exactly as it is and do not attempt repairs. Bank statements, order histories, photos, and medical records can often fill gaps, and an attorney can help gather what is still available.
